query: what ranking function scores documents using term saturation and length normalization
how do I merge results from lexical and embedding retrievers without calibrating scores
reference_answer: Use reciprocal rank fusion, which sums 1/(constant+rank) across lists.

query: why can a reranker not fix a retriever that misses the relevant document
reference_answer: A reranker only reorders first-stage candidates, so first-stage recall caps its performance.

query: what are the risks of letting an LLM decide when to stop searching
reference_answer: Runaway loops, redundant searches, higher latency and cost; use step budgets and stopping criteria.

query: compare BM25 and dense retrieval on rare entities and paraphrases
reference_answer: Dense handles paraphrase and vocabulary mismatch but can miss exact identifiers and rare entities, where BM25 is robust.

query: can I trust an LLM judge's scores
reference_answer: Only after calibrating against human labels, because of position, verbosity and self-preference biases.

query: how to measure whether a search change helped real users
reference_answer: Run A/B tests or interleaving on online metrics, and check offline metrics like nDCG correlate with them.

query: trade off between caching freshness and consistency
reference_answer: Caches speed up repeated head queries but invalidation must balance freshness against consistency.
